title: Hardware Requirements
description: Required hardware for building a PayDeck point-of-sale device including the ESP32-2432S028R display module.
text: getting started hardware requirements everything you need to build your paydeck device. the total cost is typically around $10, with most components available from common electronics retailers. esp32-2432s028r module paydeck runs on the esp32-2432s028r, commonly known as the "cheap yellow display" (cyd). this compact module combines an esp32 microcontroller with a 2.8" touchscreen, providing everything needed for a point-of-sale terminal in one board. esp32-2432s028r what's included on the board finding the right module search for esp32 2.8 inch tft touch . note whether listings show single or dual usb ports, as this determines which display driver your board uses. technical specifications component specification additional hardware board versions & display drivers the esp32-2432s028r exists in multiple hardware versions with different display controller ics. this is critical because each requires a different driver configuration in platformio. version usb ports display driver platformio environment single usb ili9341 esp32dev-hspi-ili9341-2v8 dual usb esp32dev-hspi-st7789-2v8 how to identify your board count the usb ports on your board. paydeck configuration paydeck firmware includes build environments for both variants. select the correct environment in platformio.ini based on your board version. see building firmware for details. usb-to-serial chips independent of the display driver, boards also vary in their usb-to-serial chip, which affects driver installation: see usb drivers for installation instructions. incompatible modules these similar-looking modules will not work with paydeck firmware: paydeck supports both ili9341 and st7789 display variants of the esp32-2432s028r. make sure to select the correct build environment for your specific board version. enclosure while not required, an enclosure protects the device and gives it a professional appearance for customer-facing use. where to buy buying tips buy from sellers with good reviews and multiple orders consider ordering 2–3 units for backup or in case of defects verify the exact model number: esp32-2432s028r note whether it has single or dual usb ports (affects driver selection) both layouts are supported: dual-usb boards (usb-c + micro-usb) use the st7789 image, single micro-usb boards use the ili9341 image got your hardware? next, set up your development environment with the required software. software setup coming soon display 2.8" processor dual-core wifi built-in power 5v via usb esp32-wroom-32 (dual-core 240mhz) 2.8" tft display (320×240) ili9341 or st7789 display driver xpt2046 resistive touchscreen usb for power & programming (usb-c on dual-usb boards) wifi 802.11 b/g/n sd card slot (unused) rgb status led esp32-wroom-32, 240mhz dual-core xtensa lx6 memory 520kb sram, 4mb flash 2.8" tft, 320×240 pixels, 65k colors ili9341 (v1/v2) or st7789 (v3) touch connectivity wifi 802.11 b/g/n (2.4ghz), bluetooth 4.2 ble power input 5v via usb (usb-c or micro-usb) power draw ~180–250 ma typical, up to ~350 ma peak (wi-fi) dimensions 86mm × 50mm × 10mm (board only) usb data cable usb cable that fits your board (usb-c on dual-usb boards, micro-usb on single-usb boards) for programming and power. must be a data cable, not charge-only. usb power adapter a 5v usb adapter rated 1a or more. for permanent installation. common on chinese-sourced modules silicon labs chip 3d print your own download a community case model for this board from printables and print it at home or through a local print service. buy pre-made order a ready-to-use enclosure from etsy. ships worldwide. aliexpress amazon if your device isn't recognized, try a different cable. this is the most common issue. the device draws roughly 180–250 ma, with peaks up to about 350 ma while wi-fi transmits. any phone charger will work. requires ch340 driver installation driver often pre-installed on windows/macos 3.5" display with different resolution and pin configuration different processor architecture (esp32-s3 vs esp32-wroom) generic esp32 + separate display different wiring and pin mappings open the model on printables

title: Web Flasher
description: Flash PayDeck firmware onto your ESP32 directly from the browser. No drivers, no IDE. Works in Chrome and Edge.
text: install flash from your browser manual installation guide what happens during install hardware requirements first-boot guide if something goes wrong matching driver secure build guide verify the firmware gitlab releases page verify locally check the maintainer's signature sha256sums file, which is signed with the maintainer's openpgp key. the application starts 65,536 bytes (0x10000) into the merged image and runs to the end of the file, so its hash can be computed straight from the file you downloaded here. pick the display driver plug the esp32 into a usb port press and hold the boot button click connect & flash, then pick the port release boot once the chip is detected wait roughly two minutes continue setup on the device the port picker is empty or doesn't show the cyd read timeout / "failed to connect with the device" "the port is already open" the screen stays white, or the colours are inverted or garbled can i flash a secure or production build from here? ili9341, single usb board use a data-capable cable. some cheap cables only carry power and won't show up in the browser's port picker. small tact switch on the back of the cyd, next to the usb connector. holding it pulls gpio0 low so the chip enters rom download mode at the next reset. required on every flash — auto-reset alone is unreliable on most cyd clones. with boot still held, click the install button above. the browser shows a usb device picker and grants the page access only to the port you select. about 2 seconds after the picker closes, the flasher reports the chip and begins writing. from this point you can release boot and let it run. the flasher erases the chip, writes the bootloader, partition table, and application image, then verifies. don't unplug the device or close the tab. the chip didn't enter download mode. hold the boot button before clicking the install button and keep it held until the flasher reports the chip. if that doesn't work, hold boot, briefly press reset (or en), then release boot — that walks the chip into download mode regardless of what the usb-serial chip does. a previous attempt left the serial port locked. close any other tabs or programs that might be using it (arduino serial monitor, platformio, screen, minicom), unplug and replug the device, then retry. the firmware is running but the wrong panel driver was chosen. flash the other variant: st7789 for the dual-usb board, ili9341 for the single-usb board. nothing is damaged by trying the wrong one.

title: Building Firmware
description: Clone the PayDeck repository and build firmware using PlatformIO.
text: installation building firmware clone the paydeck repository, understand the build environments, and flash the firmware to your device. estimated time: 5-10 minutes (first build), under 1 minute (subsequent) step 1: get the source code download zip extract to a folder on your computer step 2: open in vs code platformio may take a minute to scan the project and download dependencies on first open. wait until the status bar shows "platformio: ready". step 3: understand build environments paydeck includes several build environments with different security levels. for most users, the standard environment is recommended. the two secure environments are built with arduino as an esp-idf component and enable real, hardware-enforced protection. environment security use case esp32dev-hspi-st7789-2v8 development recommended: dual-usb boards (st7789 panel) esp32dev-hspi-ili9341-2v8 recommended: single micro-usb boards (ili9341 panel) esp32dev-idf none (idf reference) base for the secure builds esp32dev-idf-secure secure development flash + nvs encrypted, reflashable a limited number of times esp32dev-idf-release production (secure boot v2) permanent - cannot reflash ⚠️ production mode warning secure build guide recommendation: use the development environment that matches your panel: for dual-usb boards or for single micro-usb boards. since paydeck operates in watch-only mode and never stores private keys, development mode is secure enough for most use cases. the esp32dev-idf* environments are built for the st7789 (dual-usb) panel only. there is no secure or production environment for ili9341 boards. do not seal an ili9341 board with : the screen would stay white and the step cannot be undone. step 4: build and upload use the platformio terminal or command line to build and flash: development mode (recommended), dual-usb board: development mode, single micro-usb board: first boot encrypts the flash and burns dev-mode efuses. use a board you can dedicate. ⚠️ production seal (point of no return): requires chip rev ≥ 3.0 (eco3) and your own rsa signing key. do not run this until you have read the and tested thoroughly. the device cannot be reflashed afterward. the first build downloads all dependencies and compiles the firmware. this takes 5-10 minutes. subsequent builds are much faster (under 30 seconds). successful build output: if you see [success] , the firmware has been built and uploaded to the device. step 5: verify after a successful upload, the device will automatically reset and boot into paydeck. successful upload output: success! you should see the paydeck welcome screen on the display. troubleshooting firmware flashed successfully? continue to first boot to configure your device. first boot recommended clone with git recommended. allows easy updates. if you don't have git installed. open visual studio code file → open folder (or ctrl+k ctrl+o) select the "paydeck" folder you cloned/extracted wait for platformio to initialize (watch the bottom status bar) build fails with missing dependencies upload fails or times out display shows white/blank screen after flash 'no device found' error pio run -t upload -e esp32dev-hspi-st7789-2v8 pio run -t upload -e esp32dev-hspi-ili9341-2v8 pio run -t upload -e esp32dev-idf-secure ensure espressif 32 platform is installed (pio home > platforms) delete the .pio folder and rebuild run 'pio pkg update' to update all packages check usb connection and try a different port hold the boot button on the board while starting upload verify drivers are installed correctly try: pio run -t upload -e esp32dev-hspi-st7789-2v8 --upload-port /dev/ttyusb0 a white screen means the wrong panel driver; nothing is damaged single micro-usb board: flash esp32dev-hspi-ili9341-2v8 instead of esp32dev-hspi-st7789-2v8 dual-usb board: flash esp32dev-hspi-st7789-2v8 instead of esp32dev-hspi-ili9341-2v8 released builds print no serial logs; set cfg_debug to 1 in src/main.ino to get them (115200 baud) ensure usb drivers are installed (see previous page) try a different usb cable (must be data cable) check device manager / ls /dev/tty* for the port specify port manually: --upload-port com3 or --upload-port /dev/ttyusb0

title: First Boot
description: The PayDeck first-run setup wizard: choose the wallet mode, set the access password and set up the wallet, then connect to the network.
text: installation first boot a freshly flashed paydeck boots straight into a three-step setup wizard: mode, password, wallet. nothing else is reachable until it completes. this guide walks through each step. what to expect when the device powers on for the first time you see: secure and production builds on a secure or production build the very first boot takes 1-2 minutes to encrypt the flash before the wizard appears. do not disconnect power during this time or you may brick the device. setup wizard tap a row and confirm with continue. the prompt says it plainly: chosen once, cannot be changed, factory reset to start over. the mode is shown read-only under device info afterwards. password best practices type it again and save. the device shows "password saved" and locks enter the new password once on the unlock screen to reach the wallet step there is no default code and no way to skip this step. back returns to the mode picker. details in access password the "set up wallet" screen offers the same four wallet sources as wallet settings later on (wallet settings adds the privacy switch): create wallet appears only on boards with a certified tap-entropy source (the cyd has one). compare the options in wallet options setup complete an xpub import or a fixed address finishes the wizard on the spot with a "setup complete" toast. a created or restored seed finishes on the boot after the restart. either way the device lands on the home screen with the lock icon, ready to show payment qr codes. then: connect to the network paydeck starts offline: qr codes work immediately, but payments are not verified until the device is online. open the menu, enter your password and go to network settings. enter the network name (ssid) and the wi-fi password on the keypad flip the network row to online. the device connects and starts watching the blockchain only 2.4 ghz networks are supported. the network name is typed by hand (there is no list to pick from), so enter the name of the 2.4 ghz network. paydeck talks to a rostrum server (nexa's electrum implementation) over tls. default server: electrum.nexa.org:20004 run your own server verify your setup troubleshooting next steps ready to configure wifi? learn about advanced wifi settings and network configuration. wifi configuration learn more a short boot, then the 'set up paydeck' screen with two mode rows the menu corner does nothing yet: no payments, no menu, no settings until setup is done three steps in order; a power cut mid-way resumes at the first missing step choose the mode how will this device be used? receive only point-of-sale terminal watch only personal wallet monitor set the access password 8 to 128 characters, mandatory set up the wallet choose how the device gets its receiving addresses create wallet pick 12 or 24 words, tap the screen until the entropy ring is full, write the words down, verify every word, optionally add a passphrase. the device restarts when done. restore wallet enter an existing seed phrase of 12, 15, 18, 21 or 24 words, then answer the passphrase prompt. the seed is used once and erased. import xpub key type an extended public key. the seed never touches the device. enter address one fixed nexa address for every payment. wi-fi settings connect to your wireless network node settings where the device watches the blockchain home screen payment qr connection menu the wizard shows the unlock screen instead of a step picked the wrong mode password refused wi-fi will not connect cannot reach the rostrum server device stuck on the boot logo advanced network settings compare the wallet choices receiving payments create your first invoice full privacy, existing wallet privacy without a seed on the device quickest setup, no privacy shows your display name and the lock icon entering an amount shows a qr code the wi-fi icon in the top bar is green while connected, and network settings reads online, watching opens after the password; device info shows the mode a password already exists: enter it, the wizard continues at the next missing step this is also what you see after a power cut between the password and wallet steps while the wizard is still open: back from the password or wallet step returns to the mode picker after setup: more settings, factory reset, then run the wizard again no straight runs (12345678), repeated blocks (abababab) or common passwords both entries must match; the confirmation field clears on a mismatch verify the ssid and password use a 2.4 ghz network (5 ghz is not supported) move closer to the router check whether the router filters mac addresses verify wi-fi is connected and the network row says online check that your network allows port 20004 try a different rostrum server in node settings wait up to 2 minutes (secure builds encrypt the flash on first boot) released builds print no logs over serial; to see them, build from source with cfg_debug set to 1 and monitor at 115200 baud

title: USB Drivers
description: Install USB-to-serial drivers for ESP32 communication - CH340 or CP2102.

headings.text: Step 1: Check If Drivers Are Needed

text: installation usb drivers esp32 modules use usb-to-serial chips to communicate with your computer. depending on your board variant, you may need to install drivers. step 1: check if drivers are needed first, connect your esp32-2432s028r and check if it's already recognized: device detected? skip to building firmware . if not, continue below to install drivers. step 2: identify your chip the esp32-2432s028r uses one of two usb-to-serial chips: not sure which chip? try installing the ch340 driver first since it's more common. if that doesn't work, try cp2102. ch340 driver installation linux ch340 drivers are built into the linux kernel (2.6+). no installation needed. if your user can't access the port, add yourself to the dialout group: log out and back in for the change to take effect. cp2102 driver installation silicon labs provides drivers for all operating systems: windows: download and run the cp210x vcp installer macos: download the .pkg and install (allow in security settings) linux: usually built-in. same dialout group fix if needed. download cp2102 drivers step 3: verify connection success if a port appears when you connect the device, your drivers are working correctly. troubleshooting drivers working? now you're ready to build and flash the paydeck firmware. most common ch340 most common on modules from aliexpress and chinese sellers cp2102 found on some modules, often from silicon labs macos 10.15+ may require allowing the extension in security settings disconnect the esp32 from usb reconnect the device check for a new port (see step 1 commands above) note the port name (e.g., com3, /dev/ttyusb0) for later device not recognized after driver install macos blocks the driver linux permission denied on /dev/ttyusb0 port appears then disappears press win+x and select 'device manager' expand 'ports (com & lpt)' look for 'usb-serial ch340' or 'silicon labs cp210x' if you see a com port listed, drivers are working look for /dev/tty.wchusbserial* or /dev/tty.slab_usbtouart if a device appears, drivers are working run: ls /dev/ttyusb* /dev/ttyacm* look for /dev/ttyusb0 or similar linux usually has drivers built-in look for a small black chip labeled 'ch340' on the board look for a chip labeled 'cp2102' or 'silabs' download ch341ser.exe from the link below run the installer as administrator click 'install' and wait for completion download ch340 driver (windows) download ch341ser_mac.zip from the link below extract and run the .pkg installer allow the extension in system settings > privacy & security download ch340 driver (macos) sudo usermod -a -g dialout $user try a different usb cable (must be a data cable, not charge-only) try a different usb port (avoid hubs, use direct connection) restart your computer after installing drivers try the other driver (ch340 vs cp2102) open system settings > privacy & security scroll down and click 'allow' next to the blocked software if still blocked, boot into recovery mode and disable sip temporarily add your user to dialout group: sudo usermod -a -g dialout $user or use sudo for one-time access: sudo chmod 666 /dev/ttyusb0 the board may be resetting due to insufficient power try a powered usb hub or different port check if the usb cable is damaged

title: Factory Reset
description: Erase every setting, the wallet configuration and the password, and run the PayDeck setup wizard again.
text: maintenance factory reset this action cannot be undone factory reset permanently erases all device settings. afterwards you choose the wallet mode again, set a new password, set up the wallet and reconnect to the network. what gets erased when to factory reset how to factory reset method 1: from the menu duress password method 2: erase and reflash over usb if you cannot open the menu (forgotten password, device issues), erase the flash from a computer: pio run -t erase -e esp32dev-hspi-st7789-2v8 web flasher , which erases the chip before installing. use the ili9341 environment name on a single-usb board. production mode devices: after factory reset the device boots into the setup wizard and nothing else is reachable until it completes: your funds are safe ready to set up again? the first-boot guide walks through the wizard step by step. first boot guide erased not erased changing the wallet mode: it is chosen once in the wizard and cannot be edited in settings selling or giving away the device switching to a completely different wallet troubleshooting persistent issues starting fresh after testing forgot the password: the menu is locked, so use the usb method below tap menu on the home screen and enter your password open more settings and tap factory reset confirm the 'factory reset?' prompt with continue on the erase data screen type erase data on the keypad and tap erase the device erases its storage, restarts and shows the setup wizard receive only or watch only, chosen once a new access password, 8 to 128 characters create or restore a seed, import an xpub, or enter an address then, from the menu: wi-fi settings, node settings, and switch network to online (a reset device starts offline) wallet mode (receive only / watch only) and the setup state access password and the wrapped master key wallet configuration (xpub or address) privacy mode and the address index node (rostrum server) settings display name, logo, display and time preferences production mode efuses (permanent) your cryptocurrency (on the blockchain)

title: Device Settings
description: The PayDeck menu: network, wallet, device and security settings, and the transaction history.
text: maintenance device settings everything behind the menu button: network, wallet, device, password, factory reset and the transaction history. opening the menu tap the menu button in the corner of the home screen enter your access password on the keypad and tap unlock pick a category. back returns to the menu, and the menu's back returns home and locks the device again first-run setup . if you forget it, the menu, including factory reset, stays locked. the way back is a wipe: enter 15 wrong passwords in a row (the device erases itself and restarts in the setup wizard) or, on a standard build, erase and reflash over usb. menu categories things to know settings storage settings are stored in the esp32's non-volatile storage (nvs): settings persist across restarts and power cycles the account xpub is encrypted under the master key, which is wrapped by your password. the key that derives receiving addresses, a manually entered address, the wi-fi password and the node settings are encrypted with a device-bound key instead (derived from the chip id, not from the password), so the terminal can take payments while locked. on a standard build that does not stop someone who copies the flash chip factory reset, and the fifteen-strike wipe, erase all of it secure builds encrypt the whole nvs partition as well reflashing the firmware keeps the settings unless you erase the flash first need to reset everything? factory reset erases every setting and runs the setup wizard again. factory reset network settings wi-fi and node wallet settings seed, keys, privacy device settings time, display, name more settings passwords and factory reset transactions recent payments wallet mode is not a setting receive only or watch only is chosen once in the setup wizard and shown read-only in device info. changing it means a factory reset. replacing the wallet create, restore, import xpub and enter address each replace the current wallet configuration. have your backup at hand first. network changes a new wi-fi network or node takes effect when the device reconnects; a seed derivation restarts the device. password changes require the current password, because the menu itself is behind it. the device locks again after the change. wi-fi settings: network name (ssid) and password node settings: rostrum server host and port, and the wss/ws key that turns tls on or off network: switch between online (payments verified automatically) and offline (qr payments only) on a board without wi-fi this screen only states that the device is offline create wallet: new seed phrase from tap entropy (boards with a certified entropy source) restore wallet: enter an existing 12 to 24 word seed phrase, with optional passphrase import xpub key: watch-only wallet from an extended public key privacy: rotate addresses per payment, or reuse one address enter address: one fixed receiving address time settings: time zone and sync clock over the network display name: the shop name shown on the home screen home logo: choose the brand mark on the home screen display settings: brightness and auto sleep invert display: dark-on-light colours change password: set a new access password duress password: optional second password that erases the device factory reset: erase everything and run setup again device info: firmware version, hardware, wallet mode the last 15 payments with amount, time and status (older entries are overwritten) transaction detail with an explorer qr code

title: Troubleshooting
description: Common issues and solutions for PayDeck.
text: maintenance troubleshooting common issues and how to resolve them. wifi connection issues rostrum server issues display issues payment issues boot issues general tips still having issues? if none of the above solutions work: • check gitlab issues for similar problems • open a new issue with detailed description • include firmware version and hardware model • describe steps to reproduce the problem need to start fresh? factory reset erases all settings and lets you start over. factory reset can't connect to wifi wifi connects but no internet wifi disconnects frequently can't connect to rostrum server server connects but no payment detection slow payment detection screen is blank or white display colors look wrong touch not responding payment not detected wrong address displayed qr code won't scan device won't boot boot loop (keeps restarting) stuck on loading screen restart the device - solves many temporary issues check usb cable - some cables are charge-only and won't flash try development firmware first for easier debugging keep firmware updated for bug fixes factory reset as last resort (erases all settings) verify ssid and password are correct (case-sensitive) ensure you're using 2.4ghz network (esp32 doesn't support 5ghz) move closer to the router check if router has mac filtering enabled check router internet connection verify no captive portal (hotel/airport wifi won't work) check if firewall is blocking connections check signal strength (move closer to router) reduce interference from other devices try a less congested wifi channel check for router firmware updates verify server address is correct check if server is online (try in browser or telnet) ensure using wss port (usually 20004) try a different public rostrum server check if your network blocks websocket connections if the qr screen shows back / confirm / cancel, the device is in offline mode: switch menu, network settings, network to online verify wallet address/xpub is correct check if server is fully synced with blockchain try a different rostrum server server may be under load, try another check wifi signal strength network latency may be high a white screen means the image for the other panel was flashed; nothing is damaged single micro-usb board: flash the ili9341 image. dual-usb board: flash the st7789 image check if device is powered (usb connection) secure and production builds take 1-2 minutes on their first boot (flash encryption); do not cut power wrong colours mean the image for the other panel was flashed use the ili9341 image on single micro-usb title: Address Derivation
description: How PayDeck derives addresses from your seed phrase using HD wallet standards.
text: privacy address derivation how paydeck generates unlimited addresses from a single seed phrase using hierarchical deterministic (hd) wallet standards. overview hd wallets use a tree-like structure to derive keys. from a single seed phrase, you can generate billions of addresses, all recoverable from that same seed. seed phrase (12 to 24 words) master key extended public key (xpub) address 0, address 1, address 2, ... bip standards paydeck follows bitcoin improvement proposals (bips) that define how hd wallets work: nexa derivation path paydeck uses the standard nexa derivation path: component value meaning master key (root) bip44 purpose (multi-account) nexa coin type (nexa's registered number) account account index (first account) external address index (increments) the apostrophe (') means hardened derivation. hardened keys cannot be derived from the xpub alone, providing additional security. how paydeck uses this address index counter paydeck tracks which address index to use next: privacy off → m/44'/29223'/0'/0/ (always) privacy invoice 1 → m/44'/29223'/0'/0/ privacy invoice 2 → m/44'/29223'/0'/0/ ... and so on index 0 is the address used while privacy is off. turning privacy on moves to the next unused index, and the index then advances after every paid or cancelled invoice (leaving the qr screen with back keeps the same address). the counter is stored on the device and is erased by a factory reset: if you set the same wallet up again, the device starts over and hands out addresses it has used before. payments to them still arrive, but they are no longer unlinked from the earlier ones. why this matters consider the tradeoffs privacy mode has some practical considerations. learn about the tradeoffs. privacy tradeoffs mnemonic seed converts your 12- or 24-word phrase (plus the optional passphrase) into a 512-bit seed. this is the standard used by most cryptocurrency wallets. hd key derivation defines how to derive child keys from parent keys in a hierarchical tree structure. multi-account hierarchy specifies the derivation path structure for different coins and accounts. setup when you generate or import a seed, paydeck derives the xpub at m/44'/29223'/0'. the seed is then erased. address generation paydeck stores an address index counter. each new address increments this counter (0, 1, 2, 3...). privacy mode with privacy enabled, each new invoice uses the next index. without privacy, it always uses index 0. wallet compatibility your wallet software (wally, otoplo, etc.) derives addresses using the same path, so they match. recoverable all addresses can be regenerated from your seed phrase compatible works with any wallet using the same derivation path private different addresses prevent transaction linking unlimited generate billions of addresses from one seed >privacy off → m/44'/29223'/0'/0/<span classname= >privacy invoice 1 → m/44'/29223'/0'/0/<span classname= >privacy invoice 2 → m/44'/29223'/0'/0/<span classname=

title: Enabling Privacy Mode
description: How to enable and configure privacy mode in PayDeck for fresh address generation.
text: privacy enabling privacy mode use a fresh address for each payment to prevent transaction linking. privacy is off by default. requirements privacy mode requires an hd wallet setup (seed phrase or xpub). it does not work with manual address mode. why? hd wallets can derive unlimited addresses from a single seed. manual address mode only knows one address and cannot generate new ones. how to enable privacy: rotates addresses what changes after enabling once privacy mode is active: verifying it works to confirm privacy mode is working: create a new invoice note the address shown cancel and create another invoice the address should be different turning privacy off you can disable privacy mode at any time: tap the privacy row in wallet settings again and confirm with disable paydeck will use a consistent address for new invoices previously used addresses remain valid note: turning off privacy mode doesn't consolidate your funds. payments received to different addresses remain in those addresses until you move them using your wallet software. want to understand how it works? learn about hd key derivation and how paydeck generates addresses. address derivation works with does not work with open settings tap menu on the home screen, enter your password, then open wallet settings find privacy mode in wallet settings, find the row named privacy. its second line reads 'reuses address' while privacy is off toggle on tap the row and confirm 'enable privacy mode?' with enable. 'privacy enabled' appears and the row now reads 'rotates addresses'. from firmware 0.5.1 the device also moves to an address it has never shown before. without a seed or xpub the device says 'cannot enable privacy'. privacy off privacy on new invoices use fresh addresses each new payment request generates a unique address old addresses still work previously used addresses can still receive payments wallet sees all addresses your wallet software (wally, etc.) will show all derived addresses same total balance funds from all addresses are part of the same wallet restore wallet (existing seed) enter address (one fixed address) same address for every payment all transactions publicly linked simpler to track in wallet new address after every paid or cancelled invoice transactions not linked on chain

title: Privacy Tradeoffs
description: Understanding the practical tradeoffs of using privacy mode in PayDeck.
text: privacy privacy tradeoffs privacy mode provides better security but comes with practical considerations. understand the tradeoffs to make the right choice for your use case. the core tradeoff privacy mode creates multiple addresses. this provides privacy but means your funds are spread across many addresses instead of consolidated in one place. side-by-side comparison practical considerations about consolidation when you receive payments to many addresses, you may eventually want to consolidate them into fewer addresses. this is done using your wallet software (not paydeck). when to consolidate when you want to spend funds from multiple addresses when wallet performance degrades due to many utxos during low-fee periods to minimize cost privacy note: consolidation transactions link addresses together on the blockchain. this partially undoes the privacy benefits. consider this when deciding how and when to consolidate. recommendations limitations fresh addresses improve privacy but don't provide perfect anonymity: fresh addresses significantly improve practical privacy for most use cases, even if they don't provide cryptographic anonymity. summary factor privacy off privacy on simplicity better more complex none accounting easier requires wallet consolidation not needed sometimes needed ready to decide? enable or disable privacy mode based on your needs. configure privacy mode pros cons single address (privacy off) fresh addresses (privacy on) wallet complexity with privacy mode, your wallet will show many addresses instead of one. wally wallet and other hd wallets handle this automatically, but it can be visually cluttered. fund consolidation if you receive many small payments to different addresses, you may want to consolidate them periodically. this requires a transaction (with fees) that moves funds to fewer addresses. tracking income is slightly more complex when payments arrive at different addresses. most wallet software aggregates this, but manual record-keeping requires more attention. the rostrum server the device uses sees every address it asks about and can link them; running your own server avoids this consolidation transactions can link addresses timing analysis can sometimes correlate payments ip address correlation is possible without additional precautions exchange deposits may require kyc, linking addresses to identity all transactions publicly linked revenue visible to anyone transactions not linked on the blockchain revenue cannot be totalled from one address multiple addresses in wallet retail business with many customers prevents customers and competitors from seeing your transaction volume recurring payments from same payer the payer already knows about your business relationship simplicity matters more than privacy during testing reduces your profile as a target for theft depends on your comfort level with blockchain transparency

title: Why Privacy Matters
description: Understanding cryptocurrency transaction privacy and why it matters for your business.
text: privacy why privacy matters blockchain transactions are public by design. without privacy measures, every payment you receive reveals information about your business. the transparency problem nexa, like most cryptocurrencies, uses a public blockchain. every transaction is recorded permanently and visible to anyone. this transparency is great for verification and auditability, but it creates privacy challenges. what anyone can see if you use the same address for all payments, anyone who pays you can: see every payment you've ever received to that address calculate your total revenue track when you receive new payments see when and where you spend funds the problem with address reuse using one address for all payments is like publishing your bank statement online. here's what happens: real world implications the solution: fresh addresses the standard solution is to use a new address for every transaction. this breaks the link between payments: without privacy mode payment 1 → address a payment 2 → address a payment 3 → address a all payments linked. total visible to everyone. with privacy mode payment 2 → address b payment 3 → address c each payment isolated. no visible connection on the blockchain. same wallet, different addresses: all these addresses belong to the same wallet and are controlled by the same seed phrase. paydeck derives them automatically using hd (hierarchical deterministic) key derivation. how paydeck helps paydeck's privacy mode moves to a new address after every paid or cancelled invoice: when privacy matters most privacy vs. simplicity privacy mode adds complexity. each address must be monitored, and consolidating funds requires extra transactions. for some use cases, the simplicity of a single address outweighs privacy concerns. learn about privacy tradeoffs → ready to enable privacy? learn how to turn on privacy mode in paydeck. enable privacy mode business example a coffee shop uses one address. customer a pays for coffee. customer a can now see every other payment the shop has received, calculate daily revenue, and identify busy periods. personal example you receive your salary to a single address. your employer can see everywhere you spend, your other income sources, and your total wealth. competitor intelligence a competitor pays you once. they now have a window into your business: transaction volume, growth trends, and customer payment patterns. business intelligence leakage competitors can analyze your transaction patterns to understand your business performance targeted attacks criminals can identify high-value targets by analyzing blockchain wealth customer linking transactions can be correlated to identify relationships between customers spending surveillance anyone who knows your address can monitor your financial activity indefinitely new address generated for every invoice addresses derived from your xpub (no extra setup) all payments still go to the same wallet works with wally wallet and other hd wallets toggle on/off based on your needs retail businesses prevent competitors from analyzing your sales volume freelancers and contractors keep client payments separate and confidential high-value transactions avoid making yourself a target for theft recurring payments prevent payers from seeing each other's transactions any business accepting crypto basic financial hygiene, just like not publishing bank statements

title: Glossary
description: Cryptocurrency and PayDeck terminology explained.
text: reference glossary cryptocurrency and paydeck terminology explained. 0-conf (zero confirmation) a transaction that has been broadcast to the network but not yet included in a block. nexa uses double-spend proofs to make 0-conf transactions secure for most use cases. paydeck accepts payments at 0-conf, as reported by its rostrum server, and does not check double-spend proofs itself. address a string of characters that represents a destination for cryptocurrency payments. nexa addresses start with 'nexa:' followed by a cashaddr-encoded string. bip32 bitcoin improvement proposal 32. a standard for hierarchical deterministic (hd) wallets that allows deriving multiple keys from a single master seed. bip39 bitcoin improvement proposal 39. a standard for encoding cryptographic seeds as a list of words (typically 12 or 24 words), making them easier to write down and verify. bip44 bitcoin improvement proposal 44. a standard derivation path structure for hd wallets, defining how to organize accounts and addresses. block a collection of transactions bundled together and added to the blockchain. nexa produces a new block approximately every 2 minutes. blockchain a distributed ledger that records all transactions in a cryptocurrency network. each block contains a reference to the previous block, forming a chain. cashaddr an address format used by nexa (and bitcoin cash). provides error detection and is case-insensitive. confirmation when a transaction is included in a block, it receives one confirmation. each subsequent block adds another confirmation, making the transaction progressively harder to reverse. derivation path the path used to derive keys from a master seed in an hd wallet. paydeck uses m/44'/29223'/0'/0/n for nexa. double-spend an attack where someone attempts to spend the same coins twice. nexa's double-spend proofs detect and prevent this before block confirmation. double-spend proof a cryptographic proof generated by nexa nodes when a double-spend attempt is detected. this allows instant transaction security without waiting for block confirmation. efuse one-time programmable memory in the esp32 chip. once burned, efuses cannot be reset. used for secure boot and flash encryption keys in production mode. entropy randomness used to generate cryptographic keys. good entropy is essential for secure seed phrase generation. wallets in general draw it from hardware random number generators or physical dice; paydeck generates seeds only from touch-sensor noise collected while you tap the screen. esp32 a microcontroller chip by espressif with built-in wifi and bluetooth. paydeck runs on the esp32-wroom-32 module. flash encryption a security feature that encrypts all data stored in the esp32's flash memory. only available in secure build modes. hd wallet hierarchical deterministic wallet. a wallet that can generate unlimited addresses from a single seed phrase. all addresses are recoverable if you have the seed. mempool the pool of unconfirmed transactions waiting to be included in a block. nodes broadcast transactions to the mempool before miners include them in blocks. nex the native cryptocurrency of the nexa blockchain. used for all payments in paydeck. nexa a cryptocurrency focused on scalability and instant transactions. uses double-spend proofs for secure 0-conf payments. nvs (non-volatile storage) persistent storage on the esp32 that survives power cycles. paydeck stores settings, wifi credentials, and wallet configuration in nvs. password (access password) the 8 to 128 character secret set during first-run setup. it wraps the device's master key and unlocks the menu, settings and wallet. fifteen wrong attempts wipe the device. setup wizard the three-step flow a fresh or factory-reset paydeck boots into: choose the wallet mode, set the access password, set up the wallet. nothing else is reachable until it completes. wallet mode receive only (point-of-sale terminal) or watch only (personal wallet monitor). chosen once in the setup wizard and immutable afterwards; a factory reset is the only way to change it. in firmware 0.5.1 both modes behave the same apart from the label on the home screen. private key a secret number that allows spending cryptocurrency. paydeck never stores private keys (watch-only wallet). production mode paydeck's highest security configuration. enables flash encryption and secure boot permanently. cannot be reversed. qr code a two-dimensional barcode that encodes data like payment addresses and amounts. customers scan qr codes with their wallet app to make payments. rostrum a nexa blockchain indexing server. paydeck connects to rostrum servers to monitor addresses and detect incoming payments. secure boot a security feature that verifies firmware signatures before running code. prevents loading unauthorized firmware. seed phrase a list of 12 (or 24) words that encode a cryptographic seed. used to generate all keys in an hd wallet. must be kept secret and backed up safely. tls (transport layer security) encryption protocol for secure communication over the internet. paydeck uses tls/wss to connect to rostrum servers. transaction a transfer of cryptocurrency from one address to another. recorded permanently on the blockchain. utxo unspent transaction output. the basic unit of value in nexa (and bitcoin). each utxo can only be spent once. watch-only wallet a wallet that can generate receiving addresses and monitor balances but cannot spend funds. paydeck is watch-only for security. wss (websocket secure) the secure version of the websocket protocol. paydeck uses wss to maintain a persistent, encrypted connection to rostrum servers. xpub (extended public key) a special public key that can derive unlimited child public keys (addresses) without access to private keys. used by paydeck to generate receiving addresses.

title: Release Notes

title: Access Password
description: How the PayDeck access password protects the device, how it is set during first-run setup, and how to change it.
text: security access password every paydeck is protected by an access password of 8 to 128 characters. it is set during first-run setup and unlocks the menu, the settings and the wallet. what the password protects taking payments never needs the password. everything behind the menu button does: watch-only reminder: paydeck cannot spend funds, with or without the password. the password protects the device configuration. someone with menu access could point the device at their own address, which is why it matters. how it works setting the password first-run setup wizard . a fresh device cannot reach the wallet, the settings or the payment screen until a password exists, so there is no usable default code and no unprotected window: the internal provisioning default is replaced before any wallet or setting exists. choose something you can type on a phone-style keypad without looking it up. see password best practices password rules accepted rejected when set the rules apply when a password is set or changed. on the unlock screen the device simply tries what you typed. changing the password there is no option to remove the password. a financial device without a lock is not a configuration paydeck offers. duress password forgot the password? the device has to be wiped a forgotten password cannot be recovered, and the menu, including factory reset, is locked behind it. there are two ways back, and both wipe every setting, the wallet configuration and the password. enter a wrong password fifteen times in a row: the device erases itself and starts the setup wizard (the waits between attempts grow, so this takes several minutes). or, on a standard build, erase and reflash the firmware over usb. see factory reset your funds are safe. they live on the blockchain, not on the device. after the wipe the setup wizard runs again: mode, new password, wallet. production (sealed) devices cannot be reflashed, so fifteen wrong attempts are the only way to reset one. choose a strong password what makes a password strong on a device that is typed on a keypad. password best practices locked behind the password always accessible the password wraps the master key the device's master key is encrypted (aes-256-gcm) under a key derived from your password with pbkdf2. the password itself is never stored, not even as a hash: it is verified by successfully unwrapping the master key. the device locks when you return home going back to the home screen locks the vault. opening the menu asks for the password again. taking payments keeps working while locked. fifteen wrong attempts in a row wipe the device from the tenth wrong attempt the device shows how many attempts remain. on the fifteenth it erases itself to factory state. the attempt counter is saved before each check, so cutting power mid-guess does not reset it. entry is masked each character is shown as an asterisk. the last character you typed stays visible for about a second so you can catch typos, and a confirmation step guards the initial entry. new password type 8 to 128 characters on the t9 keyboard. tap a key repeatedly to cycle its letters; a tap on the text field, or a short pause, commits the pending letter. the symbol and caps keys give the full printable range, including space. next the device checks the password against the rules below. a rejected password shows a short message and lets you try again. confirm password type the same password once more and tap save. a mismatch clears the confirmation field and asks again. unlock the device shows 'password saved' and immediately locks. enter the new password once to continue with the wallet step. 8 to 128 characters letters, digits, symbols and spaces (printable ascii) passphrase style, for example several words with spaces changed at any time from more settings shorter than 8 characters ('at least 8 characters') a repeated block such as abababab or 12341234 a straight run such as 12345678 or abcdefgh common passwords such as password1, qwertyuiop or paydeck123 open the menu from the home screen and enter the current password choose more settings, then change password confirm the prompt, then enter and confirm the new password the device shows 'password saved' and returns home, locked the menu and every settings screen network, wi-fi and node configuration wallet settings (seed, xpub, address, privacy) changing the password and factory reset entering an amount and showing the qr code receiving payments and the payment status

title: Duress Password
description: An optional second password that factory-wipes PayDeck instead of unlocking it. How to set it, what it erases, and what it does not protect against.
text: security duress password an optional second password. typed on the unlock screen, it erases the device instead of unlocking it. available from firmware 0.5.1 and off by default. what it is for if someone forces you to unlock the device, you can give them the duress password instead of the real one. the device then wipes itself and restarts into the first-run setup wizard, exactly as it does after a factory reset. your wallet configuration, settings and payment history are gone from the device. paydeck is watch-only, so there are never funds on the device to protect. what the duress password protects is information that someone could read off the unlocked device: your receiving addresses, your payment history, and your wi-fi and server settings. it protects against a person using the screen, not against a person taking the device apart (see limits). setting it up tap menu and unlock with your access password. open more settings , then duress password , and confirm the “set duress password?” prompt. next , type it again and tap save the row now reads on - erases device . to turn it off, tap the row again and confirm “remove duress password?”. rules what an observer sees on the screen, nothing gives it away before it fires. the unlock screen, the wait after tapping unlock and the timing are the same whether or not a duress password is set, and nothing distinguishes the duress password from the real one until the wipe starts. the duress record never contains the device's master key, so it gives no second way into the vault. once it fires, the wipe is obvious: the device restarts into the setup wizard. if power is cut in the middle of a wipe, the device finishes the wipe on the next start instead of coming back half-erased. limits on a standard build it only helps against someone using the screen. someone who copies the flash chip instead can read the key that derives your receiving addresses, the payment history and the wi-fi password without any password, can see that a duress password is set, and can try to guess it offline. only a sealed production build closes that route. it erases the device, not the blockchain. anyone who already knows one of your addresses can still look it up on a block explorer. the wipe is permanent. you set the device up again from your own backup (seed phrase or xpub), so make sure that backup exists before you rely on this feature. a wrong guess that is neither password still counts toward the fifteen consecutive wrong attempts after which the device wipes itself anyway. do not type it to “test” it on a device you are using. it works the first time. related access password factory reset security model settings_duress_on duresssetup same rules as the access password: 8 to 128 characters, no simple patterns or common passwords. it can be set and removed only while the device is unlocked. it must be different from the access password. changing the access password clears the duress password. the device tells you, and you set it again afterwards. more settings screen with rows change password, duress password (on - erases device), factory reset and device info more settings with the duress password switched on. new duress password screen with a masked input field and a phone-style keypad entered on the same keypad as the access password.

title: Security Model
description: Understanding PayDeck security architecture including watch-only operation, TLS verification, and threat mitigation.
text: security security model paydeck is designed with security as a primary concern. this page explains the security architecture and how various threats are mitigated. watch-only architecture the fundamental security property of paydeck is that it operates as a watch-only wallet . this is the core principle behind all security decisions. the only data paydeck retains is the extended public key (xpub), which can generate receiving addresses but cannot authorize spending. network security local security brute-force self-wipe after 15 wrong password attempts the device factory-wipes itself (it warns from the 10th). the failed-attempt count is committed to storage before each attempt is checked, so power-cycling mid-guess cannot reset it. straight runs, repeated blocks and common passwords are rejected when the password is set. data storage production build encrypts the entire flash (including nvs) and locks the debug ports, which stops the dump itself — the only complete fix for at-rest attacks. the secure-development build encrypts the flash too but leaves jtag and uart download usable, so treat it as a test stage, not as protection. threat mitigation threat mitigation device theft watch-only design, password lock, 15-strike wipe forced unlock optional duress password wipes the device instead of unlocking it network eavesdropping tls encryption rogue server certificate verification firmware tampering secure boot (production mode) flash extraction flash encryption (production mode) jtag debugging jtag disable (production mode) weak randomness human tap entropy only, nist sp 800-90b measured, fail-closed limitations no security system is perfect. paydeck does not protect against: security recommendations reporting vulnerabilities report a vulnerability privately , as a confidential issue on gitlab. a confidential issue is visible only to the maintainers, so the details stay out of public view until a fix is released. please do not use a normal public issue or a chat group for this. open a confidential issue read the security policy include the firmware version or commit, the steps to reproduce, and what you expected to happen. the project aims to acknowledge a report within 5 business days and assess it within 10. please allow 30 days for a fix before publishing details. maximum hardware security learn about production mode for permanent flash encryption and secure boot. production mode no private keys private keys are never stored on the device cannot spend the device cannot sign transactions or move funds limited damage a compromised device cannot spend existing funds. it could be made to show an attacker's address for future payments, which is why the menu is locked seed erased seed phrases are used only during setup and immediately erased tls/wss encryption by default all communication with rostrum servers uses wss (websocket secure). node settings also allow plain ws, which is unencrypted and unauthenticated tls title: Secure & Production Builds
description: A complete, honest step-by-step guide to building a hardware-secured PayDeck: real flash encryption, NVS encryption, and Secure Boot V2. This burns one-time eFuses and is irreversible.

headings.text: Step 1 — Prove the app in Standard mode
Step 5 — Build and flash the production seal (one time)
What this protects — and what it doesn't

text: secure & production builds the web flasher installs the standard build only. that build is fully functional and keeps its master key encrypted under your password, but it does not encrypt the flash or lock the device to signed firmware, so someone who copies the flash chip can read the stored settings and payment history. hardware-secured device yourself. it cannot be done from a browser, and it cannot be done for you, because two things are involved that only happen on your own bench: burning efuses. flash encryption and secure boot flip one-time fuses inside the esp32 on first boot. this is physical and permanent — there is no software or hardware way to undo it. your own signing key. secure boot only runs firmware signed with a private key that you generate and keep. a shared, pre-signed image would let anyone holding that key sign malicious firmware your device would trust — so no such image exists. ⚠️ the production step is permanent and irreversible once you flash and boot the esp32dev-idf-release build, the device can never be reflashed, debugged over jtag, or returned to a normal state. read this whole page first, and prove everything works on a board you can afford to dedicate. do you even need this? paydeck is a watch-only terminal — it never holds private keys and cannot move funds. even if someone reflashed or stole a standard device, they could not spend your money. the realistic asset a secure build protects is privacy : the extended public key and receiving addresses stored in flash, plus wifi credentials. build a secure device when: the device is deployed somewhere physically untrusted. you want firmware that cannot be silently swapped or tampered with. you need at-rest confidentiality of settings and addresses. for personal use where you control physical access, the standard build is genuinely fine. build environments paydeck's platformio.ini defines these builds. the secure ones are built with arduino as an esp-idf component, so the bootloader is compiled from source with the security features actually enabled. environment flash enc. secure boot reflashable hardware esp32dev-hspi-st7789-2v8 yes any esp32 esp32dev-hspi-ili9341-2v8 any esp32 (ili9341 panel) esp32dev-idf esp32dev-idf-secure yes (dev mode) limited yes (permanent) v2 (rsa-3072) never chip rev ≥ 3.0 (eco3) development mode: it really encrypts the flash, but keeps a limited number of re-flashes and leaves jtag usable, so you can test. is the real seal. building any of these is safe. flashing and powering on the -secure -release images burns efuses. step 1 — prove the app in standard mode first make sure everything works with no security in the way. flash the standard build and complete a full run: wifi, rostrum connection, wallet setup, a real payment, and a factory reset. step 2 — test the secure stack (reversible) now prove flash encryption works, on a board you can dedicate. the first boot of this image encrypts the flash in place and burns dev-mode efuses. development mode keeps the board re-flashable, so this is the safe place to shake out problems. pio run -e esp32dev-idf-secure -t upload let the first boot finish (1–2 minutes, do not cut power). then confirm the flash is genuinely ciphertext — dump the nvs region and check it has no readable strings and high entropy: this stage is for testing the encryption stack on a board you still control. it makes a raw read of the flash chip unreadable, but jtag and uart-download decryption stay enabled and unsigned firmware still boots, so it does not protect a device that someone else can get hold of. only the permanent seal below does. step 3 — check your chip revision secure boot v2 (the rsa scheme paydeck uses) requires esp32 silicon revision 3.0 or newer (“eco3”). check yours: esptool.py --port /dev/ttyusb0 chip_id look for chip is esp32-d0wd-v3 (revision v3.x) (flash encryption), but not the secure boot v2 production seal. step 4 — generate your signing key this rsa-3072 private key is the permanent root of trust ../secure_keys/ .gitignore also blocks *.pem , so it can never be committed by accident. step 5 — build and flash the production seal (one time) the build auto-signs the bootloader and app with your key. flashing is the last time usb flashing will ever work on this board. critical: must not lose power . interrupting it can permanently brick the device. on that first boot, the firmware: enables secure boot v2, burning your key's digest and the abs_done_1 fuse. generates a unique flash-encryption key into read-protected efuse. encrypts all flash contents, including the nvs keys. disables jtag and uart-download decryption forever. reboots into the now-sealed system. step 6 — verify the seal espefuse.py --port /dev/ttyusb0 summary you should see: flash_crypt_cnt — all bits set (release mode) jtag_disable disable_dl_decrypt disable_dl_cache block1 read-protected (flash-encryption key unreadable) block2 holding your secure boot public-key digest what this protects — and what it doesn't a sealed device, verified by attacking real hardware, protects against: firmware and settings extraction — a full flash dump is ciphertext with no recoverable master key, password, wifi credentials, or addresses. jtag and uart-download attacks — disabled at the fuse level. it does protect against: sophisticated physical fault-injection (glitching) with lab equipment and physical possession — the accepted ceiling on classic esp32. logic bugs in the firmware itself. social engineering, or a lost/leaked signing key. after sealing: recovery options factory reset — erases settings, keeps firmware. still works. firmware updates — impossible. there is no ota and usb flashing is locked. bricked device recommendation: unless you have a specific threat model that needs hardware security, the standard build is the right choice. paydeck's watch-only design already means your funds are safe even if the device is reflashed or stolen.

title: Understanding Entropy
description: Deep dive into how PayDeck generates cryptographically secure random numbers for seed phrase generation using human-provided entropy.

headings.text: Why Computers Are Bad at Randomness

text: wallet understanding entropy how paydeck generates cryptographically secure seed phrases using human-provided randomness. this is how you truly "create your own" seed phrase. why this matters if an attacker can predict or recreate the random numbers used to generate your seed phrase, they can derive your private keys and steal your funds. poor randomness has led to real-world cryptocurrency thefts. understanding entropy helps you generate a truly secure seed. why computers are bad at randomness computers are deterministic machines. given the same inputs, they produce the same outputs. this is great for reliability, but terrible for generating random numbers. the solution: use a physical noise source that no algorithm can reproduce. every tap on the touch panel is read by an analog-to-digital converter whose lowest bits are genuine electrical noise, different on every read even when your finger does not move. those raw readings are the only input to your seed, and only their noisy low bits are counted toward it. isolated seed generation during seed generation, paydeck creates an isolated environment to protect your entropy: how much tapping is enough paydeck does not count taps. it counts proven bits what each tap contributes seven raw 12-bit x readings from the touch adc seven raw 12-bit y readings from the touch adc nothing else enters the seed: not the timing, not the pressure, not the hardware rng, not the clock, not the device mac. the readings are hashed in whole, so the rough position of a tap is part of the hash, but it earns no credit: only the noisy low bits are counted. each credited reading counts for a fixed fraction of a bit, set at half the min-entropy measured for this board with the nist sp 800-90b tool, so the firmware deliberately under-counts what it collects. because the entropy lives in sub-pixel sensor noise, someone filming every tap and copying your exact tap positions still cannot reproduce the seed. the guarantee is scoped to a passive observer on trusted hardware: a probe on the touch header or a tampered touch controller is a different attack, as it would be on any device. how to tap keep the sensor readings changing the seed is built only from electrical noise in the touch sensor, so a tapping pattern cannot make it predictable. what poor tapping can do is fail to earn credit: readings that repeat are not counted, and if a health test trips, the ring stops advancing and done stays disabled. tap back and start again. (if a test trips after the ring is already full, done shows “seed generation failed”.) things that do not help: good practice using dice (optional) divide the screen into 6 zones method: roll a die before each tap. tap in the zone matching the number. variation: use two dice for a 12-zone grid (2×6 or 3×4 layout). if you want dice to contribute to the seed itself, generate the seed phrase from dice with a method you trust, then use restore wallet to enter it. cryptographic mixing every reading, credited or not, is mixed into a sha-512 pool. even if some readings carry patterns, the conditioned output is uniformly distributed, and the fail-closed accounting makes sure enough genuine noise went in before anything comes out. paydeck security model comparison to other methods method entropy sources risks hardware wallet dedicated trng chip supply chain attacks software wallet os random (/dev/urandom) compromised os, malware dice rolls only physical randomness user error, calculation mistakes paydeck raw touch-sensor noise from human taps, nist-measured physical probing of the touch bus ready to generate your seed? follow the seed generation guide with these entropy principles in mind. seed generation guide pseudo-random number generators most computer 'random' numbers are calculated from a seed value using mathematical formulas. if someone knows the seed, they can predict all future numbers. hardware rng not trusted the esp32's hardware random number generator is not a certified true random source and its quality depends on the radios being active. paydeck therefore does not use it for seeds at all, not even as a mixed-in extra. predictable system state boot time, memory addresses, and internal counters can often be guessed or narrowed down by an attacker, reducing effective randomness. wifi disabled wifi is switched off while you tap. in offline mode (the default, and always during first-run setup) it stays off; on a device in online mode it can reconnect once the words are on screen, so create a wallet in offline mode if you want no radio at all until the restart. no computer required paydeck runs from any usb power source (phone charger, power bank). no computer connection needed during seed creation. immediate wipe after you verify the words and answer the passphrase question, the device derives the public key, erases the seed from memory and restarts. watch-only design paydeck has no security chip because it doesn't store secrets. only public keys (xpub) are kept after setup. holding a finger down: a held touch is read once, at the moment it lands tapping faster than ten times a second: taps closer than 0.1 s are ignored trying to tap 'randomly': position and rhythm do not affect the seed or the credit lift your finger fully between taps tap at a steady, unhurried pace keep tapping until the progress ring is full initialization the pool starts from a fixed label only. no mac address, no hardware rng, no system time collection each tap's raw x and y adc readings are hashed into the pool and credited only if they pass the repetition, proportion, autocorrelation and monotonic health tests finalization once the proven floor reaches the target (192 bits for 12 words, 320 for 24), the pool is conditioned into the 16 or 32 bytes of bip39 entropy entropy pool memory is zeroed using mbedtls_platform_zeroize() no secure element paydeck does not have a dedicated security chip (secure element). this is intentional: the device doesn't need one because it never stores private keys, seed phrases, or other critical secrets. watch-only by design after seed generation/import, only the xpub (public keys) is stored. the seed is erased as soon as the public key has been derived, and the device restarts. human input only the seed is derived from raw touch-sensor noise alone. the credit per reading is a compile-time constant from a nist sp 800-90b measurement campaign on this board; a build without a measurement credits nothing and cannot mint a seed at all.

title: Importing a Seed
description: Import an existing BIP39 seed phrase into PayDeck for watch-only address generation.

import an xpub directly so your seed never touches the device. setup time 2-3 min input 12-24 words privacy full existing wallet receive payments to addresses from a wallet you already use multiple devices use the same addresses across paydeck and your main wallet restore after reset reconfigure paydeck after a factory reset replace hardware set up a new paydeck with your existing seed select import seed from the wallet setup menu, choose 'import seed phrase'. enter your seed words use the on-screen keyboard to type each word of your seed phrase in order. the length is detected automatically. confirm import tap ok once for the whole phrase. the device checks every word and the checksum, then asks whether the seed has a passphrase. after that it derives the public key, erases the seed and restarts. derivation complete paydeck derives your xpub and immediately erases the seed from memory. stored (xpub) never stored wally wallet (recommended) otoplo any bip39/bip44 wallet word not recognized addresses don't match my wallet import fails word n is not a seed word extended public key for address derivation ability to generate unlimited receiving addresses address index counter for privacy mode your seed phrase and passphrase ensure you're using bip39 english wordlist some words look similar (e.g., 'car' vs 'card') verify the seed phrase is entered correctly check that your wallet uses the same derivation path some wallets use different address formats enter 12, 15, 18, 21 or 24 words the message names the problem: 'word n is not a seed word', 'got n words, need 12, 15, 18, 21 or 24' or 'checksum failed, check each word' verify the checksum (the last word depends on all the others)

title: Importing an xPub
description: Import an extended public key for maximum security watch-only operation.
text: wallet importing an xpub the most secure option. import an extended public key directly so your seed phrase never touches the paydeck device. maximum security with xpub import, your seed phrase never exists on paydeck , not even temporarily. you extract the xpub from your wallet software and enter only the public key. this is ideal for hardware wallet users or anyone who wants complete key isolation. what is an xpub? an extended public key (xpub) is derived from your seed phrase and allows generating unlimited receiving addresses without the ability to spend. it's the public half of your hd wallet. when to use xpub import getting your xpub limited wallet support: not all wallets allow exporting the xpub. this is an advanced feature primarily available in developer tools and some specialized wallet software. check your wallet's documentation for xpub export capabilities. paydeck needs the account-level public key of your wallet, at the nexa path m/44'/29223'/0' "extended public key" or "xpub" in wallet settings "account public key" in advanced options "watch-only export" functionality derivation path: paydeck uses m/44'/29223'/0'. the xpub must be exported for this specific path for addresses to match. alternative: if your wallet doesn't support xpub export, use import seed instead. paydeck erases the seed immediately after deriving the xpub. xpub format the format paydeck accepts is the prefix xpub_nexa: , the 33-byte compressed public key as 66 hex characters, a colon, and the 32-byte chain code as 64 hex characters. that is exactly 141 characters, all lowercase: format (placeholders, not a real key): xpub_nexa:<66 hex characters: public key>:<64 hex characters: chain code> no checksum: the key is 141 characters typed by hand, and the format has no checksum. paydeck can tell that the length and characters are right, but a single wrong digit in the chain code is accepted and produces addresses that nobody holds keys for. comparing addresses afterwards (step 4) is not optional. convert a standard xpub if your wallet or tooling gives you a standard base58 extended public key for the nexa account, this converts it to paydeck's format. it checks the key's own checksum, refuses private keys, and warns when the key is not at an account level. the converted key still has to be typed on the device by hand, and the device cannot detect a mistyped digit. compare addresses afterwards as described below. import steps tip: have your xpub visible on another screen. work through it in chunks, verifying each section before continuing. addresses match? setup complete. paydeck will generate the same addresses as your main wallet. troubleshooting security comparison method seed on device security generate seed briefly (then erased) high import xpub never maximum prefer a simpler setup? generate a seed directly on paydeck for easier setup with strong security. setup time 5-10 min privacy full what xpub can do what xpub cannot do seed phrase never touches paydeck, not even temporarily advanced users for those comfortable with wallet internals and key management business deployments staff can receive payments without access to spending keys developer setups when you have programmatic access to derive xpub from seed select import xpub from the set up wallet screen (or wallet settings later), choose 'import xpub key' enter the xpub carefully type or enter the xpub string using the on-screen keyboard tap ok paydeck checks the length, the prefix and the characters, and that the public key is a valid point. if they pass, the key is saved at once and 'wallet configured' appears; there is no separate confirmation and no restart. otherwise it shows 'key is n chars, needs 141' or 'invalid key format'. compare addresses before taking any payment, show an address on paydeck and verify that it matches the first receiving address in your wallet software invalid xpub error addresses don't match can't find xpub in wallet generate unlimited receiving addresses enable privacy mode (new address per payment) verify addresses match your main wallet compromise your private keys 'key is n chars, needs 141': characters were dropped or added; count again the key must start with 'xpub_nexa:' and contain only the hex characters 0-9 and a-f a base58 key starting with 'xpub6...' is not accepted confirm your wallet uses the correct derivation path verify derivation path is m/44'/29223'/0' some wallets use different index numbers try regenerating the xpub from your wallet most consumer wallets don't support xpub export this feature is mainly available in developer tools consider using import seed instead (seed is erased immediately) you can derive xpub programmatically from your seed using bip32 libraries
